title: verdict-runs-every-instrument-under-the-seal
intention: Codemother's verdict runs every chart instrument under the tester's instance seal, so a PROVED never executes a proof against live ~/.cairn.
why: verdict.run_instrument runs each chart criterion's instrument with bash -c and no seal; the instruments run the ticket's proofs (`python3 <proof> | ...`), so every PROVED executes proofs against live ~/.cairn — the biggest hand the census found, because it fires at every PROVED with no CC in the loop. Parent: dda0e72b9c67.
traces_to: Law 8 (a proof run must not damage the world it measures); RULE 1 (through the tester's published interface). Parent dda0e72b9c67.
how: In cairn/devices/codemother/machines/verdict/verdict.py run_instrument, run the command through the tester's published sealed exec (2c9eeab2da87: `bin/cairn test --exec <command> --timeout N`) instead of bare bash -c; keep the returned record shape (command, exit, timed_out, seconds, tail); a refusal of the seal (exit 2, no bwrap) is a recorded reading, never a bare fallback. Proof under the verdict machine's proofs/, written red.
falsifier: Done when (1) run_instrument('echo $CAIRN_TESTER_INSTANCE_SEALED') returns tail '1'; (2) an instrument that writes under ~/.cairn leaves the live file absent; (3) the record keeps its keys and an exit 3 instrument reads exit 3; (4) with the seal refused the record carries the refusal and no bare run happens. WRONG INTENT if a chart instrument measured in the standing berths legitimately needs live instance state the snapshot cannot carry.
watchme: none, because (cairn/devices/codemother/machines/verdict/verdict.py) every run's record is already berthed with the verdict packet and a seal refusal reads as a recorded failure there
children: none, because one function in one file

chart_claim.filled_by: CC chart chain (orient 275fb4eabf11 .. validate cb20da404b8f, each learned)

decisions.text: In cairn/devices/codemother/machines/verdict/verdict.py, replace run_instrument's body: argv = [os.path.join(CAIRN_ROOT, 'bin', 'cairn'), 'test', '--exec', command, '--timeout', str(timeout_s)]; subprocess.run(argv, cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout_s + 120). The timeout N is the function's own timeout_s argument (default _TIMEOUT_DEFAULT = 600, or the criterion's declared timeout_s); the +120 only bounds the tester's snapshot and teardown. --exec has no structured output: it passes the command's stdout, stderr and exit code through unchanged, so the record is built exactly as before — command (the instrument as given), exit (returncode), timed_out False, timeout_s, seconds (wall time measured here), tail (_tail of stdout + stderr). Two tester lines on stderr are read by prefix: exit 124 with a line starting 'cairn test --exec: timed out after' sets exit None and timed_out True; exit 2 with a line starting 'cairn test --exec: refused' adds seal_refused = that line and keeps exit 2. Nothing else is forked in either case — never a fallback to bash -c. The existing TimeoutExpired and OSError arms stay as they are.
decisions.step: unlisted: edit verdict.py run_instrument to invoke bin/cairn test --exec instead of subprocess.run bash -c
